acceptance_criteria: All integration tests in JMAP-pdb and JMAP-klj pass against MemoryMdnBackend
description: Add MemoryMdnBackend to the test harness in tests/. Canonical example for implementors; also used by all MDN integration tests.
design:
Storage needs: access to the same blob store and email store as MemoryMailBackend — share or reference the same Arc<Mutex<Store>>.

send_mdns implementation:
  For each entry in the send map:
    1. Fetch the email by for_email_id from the email store. If not found, add notFound SetError.
    2. Check the email has a Disposition-Notification-To header. If absent, add notFound SetError (per spec §2.1).
    3. Build a fake RFC 5322 MDN message (in-memory bytes — no real SMTP). Store the generated message bytes as a new blob.
    4. Populate server-set fields: original_message_id from the source email's Message-ID header, original_recipient from the Original-Recipient header if present, final_recipient derived from the identity's email address, mdn_gateway = None (not a gateway), error = None.
    5. Add to sent map with only the server-set fields.
  Return MdnSendResult.

parse_mdns implementation:
  For each blob_id:
    1. Look up blob bytes. If not found, add to not_found.
    2. Attempt to parse as multipart/report containing a message/disposition-notification part.
       For test purposes: a blob is parsable if it contains the ASCII string 'Disposition:' (minimal heuristic — document this).
       A real implementation would use a MIME parser.
    3. If parsable: extract fields and build Mdn. Look up originalMessageId in sent email store to populate forEmailId.
    4. If not parsable: add to not_parsable.
  Return MdnParseResult.

Test fixtures: pre-build a valid MDN blob constant (hand-crafted RFC 5322 bytes matching draft §3.3 example) and an invalid blob constant. These must be hand-written, not generated by the code under test.
title: mdn: MemoryMdnBackend for tests
